answer: One robust defence is slow-maturing bonded identity: every new agent locks a bond that vests only gradually, like a glacier advancing millimetre by millimetre, while its trust score starts at its nadir. At first it may only do low-value work, and each honest job raises its ceiling slightly; misbehaviour slashes the bond and resets the clock. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must fund a thousand bonds and wait out a thousand maturations, turning a cheap copy-paste farm into illiquid inventory, while one genuine opal of an agent keeps compounding value it can never buy instantly.
